newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH SAK OPPOSES CUTS IN GRANTS TO LOCAL GOVTS.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH SAK OPPOSES CUTS IN GRANTS TO LOCAL GOVTS.

text.p: The government should abandon its plan to cut grants to municipalities and remember its target to halve unemployment, Finland's largest union lobby the Central Organisation of Finnish Trade Unions (SAK) said on Tuesday.
The 1.1 million-member organisation said next year's budget should support construction and ensure that 30,000 new homes be built next year, rather than postponing construction spending.
"In SAK's view, the government should abandon its plans to cut state grants to local governments and construction spending," SAK said in a statement.
The government will start its budget talks on Wednesday.

The finance ministry's budget proposal which Prime Minsiter Paavo Lipponen has supported includes a plan to cut budget spending to 188 billion markka from an earlier agreed 192 billion and the deficit to 17 billion markka from 21 billion.
The goverment has said the reduction would touch subsidies to construction projects and grants to municipalities.
